task: Ticket order survey: adversarial scenarios (design-level ruling out; independent confirmation pending EVL and the read-only reviewer).

scenarios.scenario: Attacker attaches a survey to another user's order by sending a foreign user id or order id
scenarios.rationale: Route passes p_user_id only from the authenticated session; the upsert checks orders(id, user_id) and raises the same P0002 for a missing order and a foreign order; the table has a composite FK (order_id, user_id). Covered by the SQL tests and route tests; hosted DB unverified.

scenarios.scenario: anon/authenticated caller invokes the new SECURITY DEFINER functions or reads/writes ticket_order_survey directly through the public API
scenarios.rationale: All four functions and the table are revoked from public, anon and authenticated and granted to service_role only; RLS is on; runner asserts exact signatures and 42501 under set role. The owner must re-run the SQL verification queries after applying on the hosted DB.

scenarios.scenario: Out-of-list, duplicate, empty, mistyped or prototype-name survey ids (constructor, __proto__, toString, hasOwnProperty) are submitted to bypass validation
scenarios.rationale: Client validation, server parseSurvey (exact three keys, allowlisted ids, Object.hasOwn/Map lookups) and DB CHECKs through the IMMUTABLE helper; invalid input returns the generic 400 with zero RPC calls.

scenarios.scenario: Slow or hanging survey save delays or blocks checkout (denial of service on the payment path)
scenarios.rationale: Save is a never-rejecting promise started in parallel with PayOS and joined with a 1500 ms capped race; timer cleared in finally; 201 with the payment link is always returned. Mechanism proven by mocked tests and benchmark; hosted latency and serverless freeze after response are NOT proven (K.1).

scenarios.scenario: Logs, errors or Server-Timing leak order ids, user ids or survey answers
scenarios.rationale: Log is only console.error with reason and code; no new Server-Timing names; route tests stringify the log and assert absence of ids and answers.

scenarios.scenario: Worker marks an order synced with blank survey cells after a read failure, silently losing the answers
scenarios.rationale: Worker treats an empty array as no survey (blank cells) but any rpc error, throw, non-array, malformed or multi-row result as survey_read_failed: nothing written, not completed, failed through the existing path. Late-arriving survey after sync remains a known race (AC20) fixable by the service_role-only requeue function.

scenarios.scenario: Old 14-column app or old PayOS webhook syncs into the 17-column Sheet during cutover, or a deployed app keeps a 14-column range
scenarios.rationale: Mitigated, not eliminated: new code rejects the previous range fail-closed (invalid_range); the runbook forbids calling sync/enqueue before the new app deploys and requires expired PayOS links with checkout off. Depends on the owner following the runbook; pre-cutover rows would duplicate on re-sync.

scenarios.scenario: Spreadsheet formula or injection through survey values
scenarios.rationale: Values written are fixed labels mapped from allowlisted ids and sent with valueInputOption RAW as before; free text is not accepted.

scenarios.scenario: Probe window sends a real customer's order to the Sheet copy
scenarios.rationale: Residual operational risk documented in the runbook (reconcile paid orders in the window, use the requeue function for orders with a survey); owner decision.

scenarios.scenario: Survey data sent to a third-party Sheet without consent or retention rules
scenarios.rationale: Named debt, undecided by the owner; must be resolved before real ticket sales.
